hook.line: When you need something from an office, a bank or a board, asking nicely is not enough: the request has to sound official. One verb does the job, and it is the one you will see on every form.
hook.en: I request a review of the file.

examples.en: I request a review of the file.

examples.en: We request your permission to use your name.

examples.es: Solicito una cita con la directora.
examples.en: I request an appointment with the director.
I request a copy of the contract.
We request the approval of the regulations.

examples.en: I request permission to close the café.

rule:
*Solicitar* is the written, official "to ask for". It is followed directly by what you want: *Solicito una copia del contrato*. There is no *para* in front of the thing.

The formal touch is to name the request as a noun: *la revisión del expediente*, *la aprobación del reglamento*, rather than "that you review the file".

To ask for permission to do something, use *su autorización para* or *permiso para* + plain verb: *Solicitamos su autorización para usar su nombre*.

At a counter or among friends, nobody says *solicito*. There you say *¿Me regala…?* or *¿Me da…?*. Keep *solicito* for letters, forms and boards.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the institutional register of requesting. The noun after *solicito* is usually a nominalisation of a verb.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Solicitar* takes what you want directly, with no *para*.

pitfalls.right: Solicitamos su autorización para usar su nombre.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Para* links the permission to what it is for.
